label: CJEU C-340/21 — VB v NAP (breach, fear-of-misuse damage)
body: 1. Unauthorised disclosure of, or access to, personal data by a third party is not, in itself, sufficient to conclude that Art. 24/32 technical and organisational measures were inappropriate. Appropriateness is assessed concretely against the risks.
3. In an Art. 82 action, the controller bears the burden of proving its security measures were appropriate under Art. 32.
5. The controller is not exempt from Art. 82 compensation merely because the damage resulted from third-party unauthorised access; the controller must prove it is "in no way responsible".
6. Fear of possible misuse by third parties following an infringement can in itself constitute non-material damage under Art. 82(1).
Why it matters: Breaches expose the controller to damages claims even without proven misuse. Plaintiffs only need a well-founded fear. Aggressive Art. 32 documentation is the only defence.
